github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGenerat.text: Return only one commit message on one line, without Markdown or quotation marks. Use `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, or `<type>: <subject>` when no scope applies. Describe the staged changes, not unrelated changes. Obey the applicable repository commitlint rules, also those from inherited configurations. These rules take precedence over the defaults below. Use a scope only when it accurately identifies the affected component. Write the subject in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100). Start the subject with an imperative verb. Use short, direct words and keep necessary articles. Use lowercase prose, but keep the exact case of technical names and identifiers. Do not end the subject with a period. Use `!` before the colon for a breaking change. Do not add a body, footer, attribution, or trailer, such as `Co-authored-by`. Allowed types and scopes are listed in ~/.commitlintrc.json. Choose the type from the changed path, and add the scope of the tool when one fits. Use `agents` for agent configuration, `zsh(plugin|theme)` for Zsh files, and `shell` for other shell files. Use `macos(defaults|launchd)` for system preferences and launch agents, `git(gh|glab)` for Git, and `gui(ghostty)` for desktop apps. Use `editor`, `brew`, `node`, `ruby`, or `python` for their tools, and `chore` for repository-wide files. A commit that changes only a Zsh integration uses `zsh(plugin)`.
